reasons: Both answers make the same core recommendation: native logical replication, a short freeze, fixing sequences and setting up reverse replication for rollback. Both explain concretely why dual-write is not atomic and why backfill races cause drift. B edges ahead because it has a dedicated continuous verification phase (per-range checksums and shadow reads), names upsert-if-newer for idempotency, and explicitly drops the forward subscription at cutover, while A does not handle the forward subscription when adding reverse replication (though A's Django QuerySet.update/bulk detail is a nice touch).
